text.title: Ramp Task Difficulty Ladder Output Contract
text.summary: Draft-07 JSON Schema for `RampLadder`: a header with owner, ramp window, review cadence and tracker label prefix; at least 4 rungs each defined by observable scope, a duration band, a fading buddy-support level, evidence from a completed prior ramp (or `not_applicable: unvalidated`) and at least 2 tagged tickets kept off the critical path on rungs 1-2; per-newcomer ramps recording rung-by-rung merges with no skips and overrun reclassification; and an outcome review that records `time_to_first_pr`, the rung reached, and re-bands out-of-band rungs. Validator: `scripts/validate-ramp-task-difficulty-ladder.py`.

section.title: JSON Schema (draft-07)
section.note: What the validator's cross-field block checks beyond the schema: rungs are numbered 1..n without gaps; `expected_duration_days.max` is at least `min`, non-decreasing up the ladder, and the top rung's `max` is at most `header.ramp_window_days` (r-durations-monotonic-rung1-under-a-day); `buddy_support` never increases up the ladder and the top rung is `scheduled_check_ins` (r-buddy-support-fades-per-rung); every rung's tagged-ticket labels start with `header.rung_label_prefix` followed by the rung number (r-tickets-tagged-before-start-date); in each ramp, `tickets_tagged_on` is on or before `start_date`, the progression starts at rung 1 and never rises by more than one rung per merged ticket, and any ticket whose `actual_duration_days` exceeds twice its rung's `max` carries `reclassified_to_rung` (r-rung1-merges-to-main, r-tickets-tagged-before-start-date, r-promotion-requires-completed-rung); in the outcome review, `within_band` agrees with the rung's band, a rung out of band for two or more consecutive cycles is re-banded or rewritten with `version_bumped` true, `median_time_to_first_pr_days` above 3 requires an action on rung 1, and `next_due` is at most 31 days (monthly) or 92 days (quarterly) after `last_run` (r-outcome-review-regrades-rungs, r-rung1-merges-to-main).

example.note: Subject violations: rung names and examples are story points and "easy / medium" (r-rung-defined-by-observable-scope); rung 1's upper bound is 2 days and rung 4's 12-day upper bound exceeds the 10-day ramp window (r-durations-monotonic-rung1-under-a-day); rung 1's evidence is a PR on an onboarding-kata repo and rung 2's is the tech lead's own PR (r-rung1-merges-to-main, r-evidence-is-a-completed-prior-ramp); buddy support drops to check-ins at rung 2 and rises again at rung 3 (r-buddy-support-fades-per-rung); a rung-1 ticket on the critical path with a deadline inside the window, rung 2 with one tagged ticket, and tickets tagged the day after the start date (r-tickets-tagged-before-start-date); the newcomer jumped from rung 1 to rung 4 and the 4-day rung-1 ticket was never reclassified (r-promotion-requires-completed-rung); rung 1 out of band for two cycles with no action, median time to first PR of 5 days with nothing changed, `within_band` true on a rung-4 median of 9 against a 3-12 band that itself breaks the window, and the next review 6.5 months out (r-outcome-review-regrades-rungs).

antipattern.description: A rung `name` or `ticket_pattern.examples` entry naming story points, T-shirt sizes or easy / medium / hard, or a pattern without files, modules, flag and design-review fields.
antipattern.reason: r-rung-defined-by-observable-scope: story points encode the estimator's familiarity, not the newcomer's difficulty.

antipattern.description: Fewer than 4 rungs, `expected_duration_days.max` decreasing up the ladder, rung 1 `max` above 1 day, or a top rung `max` beyond `ramp_window_days`.
antipattern.reason: r-durations-monotonic-rung1-under-a-day: a ladder not ordered by effort is a list; day one must end with something merged.

antipattern.description: Rung 1 evidence whose `merged_ref` is a kata, training repo or unmerged branch, or a `median_time_to_first_pr_days` above 3 with no action on rung 1.
antipattern.reason: r-rung1-merges-to-main: a training repo teaches the newcomer the training repo.

antipattern.description: `buddy_support` identical across rungs, increasing up the ladder, rung 1 other than `full_pairing`, or the top rung other than `scheduled_check_ins`.
antipattern.reason: r-buddy-support-fades-per-rung: support that never fades produces a newcomer who can only work while paired.

antipattern.description: Evidence `validated` without a merged ref, a newcomer name and an actual duration; a senior engineer's PR as evidence; or an unvalidated rung without `not_applicable: unvalidated`.
antipattern.reason: r-evidence-is-a-completed-prior-ramp: bands invented at a whiteboard are wrong in the same direction every time.

antipattern.description: Fewer than 2 `tagged_tickets` on any rung, a rung-1 or rung-2 ticket with `on_critical_path` or `deadline_inside_ramp_window` true, or `tickets_tagged_on` after `start_date`.
antipattern.reason: r-tickets-tagged-before-start-date: day one spent watching the buddy scroll Jira.

antipattern.description: A `progression` that does not start at rung 1 or rises by more than one rung per merged ticket, or an overrun past twice the band with no `reclassified_to_rung`.
antipattern.reason: r-promotion-requires-completed-rung: seniority shortens each rung, it does not remove them.

antipattern.description: A rung `within_band: false` with `action: none`, two consecutive out-of-band cycles without `version_bumped`, `within_band` that disagrees with the band, or `next_due` beyond the cadence.
antipattern.reason: r-outcome-review-regrades-rungs: without the regrade the ladder drifts away from the codebase it describes.

text.reference: Stdlib-only validator for this contract; `--self-test` runs both examples above.
Markdown ladder skeleton with the same header keys, rung columns and review fields.
